title: Contactless Electric Current Sensing Using Drone-Integrable Sensor
author: Osmani, Schulz

steps.title: Install Autodesk EAGLE
steps.instruction: Download Autodesk EAGLE from http://www.autodesk.com/products/eagle/free-download, select the installer for your OS, verify system requirements, run the installer, accept the license, complete installation, launch EAGLE, sign in with an Autodesk account (free personal‑use license activates automatically).

steps.title: Create Project and Schematic
steps.instruction: Start a new project (e.g., "Schematic"), create a new workspace in the Control Panel, note the free version limits: 2 schematic sheets, 2 signal layers, 80 cm² board area.

steps.title: Design Custom Component Libraries
steps.instruction: Create symbols and footprints for each required part using the Library Editor, then map pins to pads and save the devices.

substeps.instruction: DRV5055A1: open EAGLE 9.6.2 control panel, create new symbol (VCC, OUT, GND), create TO‑92 footprint with three pads, draw silkscreen, map pins, save.
MAX280CWE+: create new symbol with pins per datasheet, create SOIC‑16 Wide footprint with 16 pads, draw silkscreen, map pins, save.
LTC6900CS5#TRMPBF: create new symbol, create SOT‑23‑5 footprint with 5 pads, draw silkscreen, map pins, save.
BD50GA5MEFJ‑LBH2: create new symbol, create HTSOP‑J8 footprint with 9 pads, draw silkscreen, map pins, save.
BD80GC0VEFJ‑ME2: create new symbol, create HTSOP‑J8 footprint with 9 pads, draw silkscreen, map pins, save.

steps.title: Add Generic Two‑Terminal Devices
steps.instruction: Create a generic two‑pin symbol (terminals “1” and “2”), design a matching footprint with standard pad spacing, draw silkscreen outline, map pins, and save the library component for resistors, capacitors, connectors, etc.

steps.title: Layout PCB and Place Mounting Holes
steps.instruction: Arrange components on a two‑layer board (top and bottom) respecting the following placement rules and design constraints.

substeps.instruction: Place wire connectors at board edges for cable routing.
Place DC‑DC converters at the bottom, allocating a common ground area.
Center the low‑pass‑filter (LPF) circuitry.
Set control‑signal trace width ≥25 mil, power‑signal trace width ≥50 mil.
Use two‑layer configuration only.
Insert round circles for 6 mm bolts to enable vertical stacking of eight PCBs (one per MF sensor).
Run ERC and DRC checks, then generate Gerber, drill, and netlist files for manufacturing.

steps.title: Wire Component Connections on PCB
steps.instruction: Connect the components on the schematic/PCB exactly as listed (a–j).

substeps.instruction: a. Connect DRV5055A1 output to ERA‑8ARW2942V.
b. Connect the other ERA‑8ARW2942V terminal to the FB input of MAX280CWE+ via capacitor VJ0805Y154JXXTW1BC and also to the OUT pin of MAX280CWE+ through a second VJ0805Y154JXXTW1BC.
c. Connect both terminals of each VJ0805Y154JXXTW1BC to terminal block 1729128.
d. Place C1206X104J8HACTU between VCC and GND of the DRV5055A1.

e. Connect DRV5055A1 GND to TAJA106J010RNJ, Y112125K0000T9R, and the V‑ pin of MAX280CWE+. Connect the other terminals of TAJA106J010RNJ and Y112125K0000T9R to the AGND pin of MAX280CWE+, Y112125K0000T9R, and the OUT pin of MAX280CWE+ through RN73H1JTTD3523D100.
f. Connect +5 V to the DIVIDER_RATIO pin of MAX280CWE+ and to the floating terminal of Y112125K0000T9R.
g. Connect the Cosc pin of MAX280CWE+ to the OUT pin of LTC6900CS5#TRMPBF.

h. Connect the V+ pin of MAX280CWE+ to the DIV pin of LTC6900CS5#TRMPBF, to C1206X104J8HACTU, and to ERA‑8AEB364V; connect the other terminals of C1206X104J8HACTU and ERA‑8AEB364V to GND and to the SET pin of LTC6900CS5#TRMPBF respectively.
i. Connect GND pins of LTC6900CS5#TRMPBF, BD50GA5MEFJ‑LBH2, and BD80GC0VEFJ‑ME2 together; ensure all GNDs share the common ground of the 3S1P (12 V) 5000 mAh battery.

j. Connect VCC and GND of the 3S1P battery to Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 of the 1729128 terminal block; route Terminal 1 to VCC pins of both BD50GA5MEFJ‑LBH2 and BD80GC0VEFJ‑ME2; connect two TAJW225K050RNJ resistors (one to VCC, one to Vo) for each of those ICs; tie the negative terminals of the four TAJW225K050RNJ resistors and the GND pins of both BD50GA5MEFJ‑LBH2 and BD80GC0VEFJ‑ME2 to the common circuit ground.

steps.title: Run ERC/DRC and Export CAM Files
steps.instruction: Perform Electrical Rule Check (ERC) and Design Rule Check (DRC) to confirm a error‑free layout, then generate the required CAM data (Gerber files, drill files, assembly files) for PCB manufacturing.

steps.title: Fabricate PCB According to Specifications
steps.instruction: Follow the detailed fabrication workflow, keeping all dimensional tolerances and material specifications.

substeps.instruction: Import Gerber, drill, and netlist files into CAM350.
Run a full Design‑for‑Manufacturability (DFM) check using Valor NPI; verify power trace width 50 mil, control trace width 25 mil, clearances, and drill sizes ≥0.3 mm.
Create high‑resolution photoplot films for each copper layer, solder mask, and silkscreen with an Orbotech Diamond 10 laser photoplotter (alignment ±25 μm).
Clean FR‑4 panels, apply photoresist with a roll laminator, align photoplots, and expose using an LPKF ProtoLaser LDI UV system.
Develop and etch to form conductor patterns.
Perform Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) with an Orbotech Discovery Ⅱ 9000 system.
Stack inner layers with prepregs and cores; laminate under controlled temperature/pressure in a Burkle multi‑layer press.
Drill plated‑through holes, vias, and mechanical holes using a Schmoll CNC drilling machine.
Deposit electroless copper, then electroplate ~25 μm copper in an Atotech metallization line.
Repeat photoimaging on outer layers, electroplate copper traces again, and etch unprotected copper to achieve final copper thickness of 35–70 μm.
Apply solder mask with a curtain coater, expose and develop pad openings with UV, print silkscreen legends using an Orbotech inkjet printer (line width ≥0.15 mm).
Apply final ENIG surface finish via an Atotech ENIG line.
Test electrical continuity with an ATG Luther & Maelzer flying‑probe tester.
CNC‑profile the panels using an LPKF ProtoMat S104.
Finish with visual inspection and thickness measurement.

steps.title: Apply Solder Paste and Populate PCB
steps.instruction: Populate the fabricated boards using automated solder‑paste and component‑placement equipment, then reflow and inspect.

substeps.instruction: Secure the PCB in an EKRA X5 stencil printer, align a stainless‑steel stencil, and squeegee solder paste onto all pads.
Load the PCB into a Mycronic MY300 pick‑and‑place machine; verify component placement via optical recognition and fiducial alignment.
Transfer the populated board through a Heller 1809 MK5 reflow oven on a conveyor belt.
Inspect the reflowed board with a CyberOptics SQ3000 AOI system; perform X‑ray inspection of BGA devices with a Nikon XT V 160.
Conduct functional electrical testing to confirm circuit operation.

steps.title: Connect Arduino and Peripheral Modules
steps.instruction: Wire the assembled PCBs to the Arduino Mega 2560 and supporting modules as follows.

substeps.instruction: Connect all DRV5055A1 GND pins to the Arduino Mega 2560 GND and to the common circuit ground.
Connect DS3231MPMB1# GND to the common ground; wire its SCL to Arduino pin 21 and SDA to pin 20.
Connect the SPI microSD card module GND to common ground, VCC to +5 V, CS to Arduino pin 10, SCK to ICSP pin 3, MOSI to ICSP pin 4, and MISO to ICSP pin 1.
Power the Arduino via the BD80GC0VEFJ‑ME2 regulator at +8 V.
Mount each DRV5055A1 sensor inside two adjacent fastening tubes of the sensor box (tube inner diameter <2 cm); route its 3‑wire (VCC, GND, VOUT) cable to the corresponding SPU header.

steps.title: Program Arduino for Data Acquisition
steps.instruction: Upload firmware that reads the DRV5055A1 outputs, applies a 10‑bit ADC, uses voltage dividers to keep signals ≤5 V, filters with a 55 Hz low‑pass filter, timestamps each sample with the DS3231RTC, and writes timestamp (hh:mm:ss) and filtered voltage to a 32 GB microSD card via SPI.

steps.title: Analyze and Visualize Recorded Data
steps.instruction: Insert the microSD card into a computer, open the Excel file containing two columns (timestamp in hh:mm:ss and voltage), import the data into MATLAB, compute RMS current values, and generate plots of current versus time.

description: This protocol outlines a comprehensive approach for developing a drone-mounted electrical sensor designed for contactless current measurement in overhead Transmission Lines (TLs). The sensor system consists of an encapsulating unit (i.e., sensor box) that houses dedicated Signal Processing Units (SPUs). These SPUs process the captured Magnetic Fields (MFs) generated by the current flowing through the TL and convert them into computer-readable data. The resulting voltage signals are then fed into an Arduino Mega 2560. Using a Real-Time Clock (RTC)-based circuit, these sensed voltages accurately reflect the original current-inducing signals and are subsequently stored on a micro–Secure Digital (SD) card along with corresponding timestamps. The primary objective is to facilitate the visualization of the Root Mean Square (RMS) values of the recorded current at any given time. To achieve this, the protocol further demonstrates how to generate MATLAB plots of the obtained results once the microSD card is inserted into a computer with MATLAB installed.
